titleText.es: Los verdaderos programadores establecen las constantes universales adecuadas para que el universo evolucione y acabe conteniendo el disco con los datos que quieren.
titleText.en: Real programmers set the appropriate universal constants so that the universe evolves and ends up containing the disk with the data they want.
titleText.noteEn: The title text extends the escalation by imagining programmers choosing the laws of physics so that the desired disk eventually exists on its own.

excludedUnits.rationale: nano is the proper name of a text editor, not Spanish vocabulary in this question.
emacs is the proper name of a text editor, retained unchanged rather than used as Spanish vocabulary.

applications.exampleEs: DEJAN QUE BATA SUS DELICADAS ALAS
applications.explanationEn: Dejan changes for the plural people granting permission, que opens the allowed action, ordinary bate changes to the requested-action form bata, and sus delicadas alas supplies what the butterfly flaps.

regions.labelEs: LA PERTURBACIÓN SE PROPAGA, ALTERANDO EL FLUJO DE LAS CORRIENTES ARREMOLINADAS DE LA ATMÓSFERA SUPERIOR.
ESTAS FORMAN BOLSAS MOMENTÁNEAS DE AIRE A MAYOR PRESIÓN
QUE ACTÚAN COMO LENTES QUE DESVÍAN LOS RAYOS CÓSMICOS, ENFOCÁNDOLOS PARA QUE INCIDAN EN EL PLATO DE LA UNIDAD Y CAMBIEN EL BIT DESEADO.

applications.exampleEs: PARA QUE INCIDAN EN EL PLATO DE LA UNIDAD Y CAMBIEN EL BIT DESEADO
applications.explanationEn: Para que introduces the intended result; incidan and cambien are the two coordinated special purpose forms, and the intervening words supply the places and things involved in those intended actions.

regions.labelEs: BONITO. POR SUPUESTO, EMACS TIENE UN COMANDO PARA HACER ESO.

excludedUnits.rationale: EMACS is the proper name of a text editor, not a Spanish lexical word.

applications.explanationEn: Por and supuesto stay together as the fixed expression that confidently treats the next point as expected.
Para introduces the purpose, and hacer remains in its unchanged -er dictionary form.

excludedUnits.rationale: This is a fictional Emacs keyboard-command sequence composed of key notation and an English command name, not Spanish vocabulary.
EMACS is the proper name of the text editor being cursed, not Spanish vocabulary.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word here; Spanish uses the article before a general group
cards.noteEn: Spanish normally uses los before a plural group discussed as a whole, as in los programadores. English often leaves “the” out and simply says “programmers” when making the same general statement.

example.es: Los perros necesitan agua.
example.en: Dogs need water.

cards.promptEs: nano, Emacs, Vim, ed y cat
cards.answerEn: Unix editing tools arranged as a one-upmanship joke about using increasingly bare-bones methods
cards.noteEn: nano, Emacs, Vim, and ed are text editors with very different interfaces. cat normally displays or joins file contents, though shell redirection can use typed input to create a file. Each speaker claims that a less comfortable, lower-level tool is what a “real” programmer would use, until the methods become physically absurd.
Oye is the informal singular command form of oír, “to hear.” In conversation it commonly gets one person's attention, like “hey” or “listen.”

example.es: Oye, necesito hablar contigo.
example.en: Hey, I need to talk to you.

cards.noteEn: Mano is feminine despite ending in -o, so it takes una and feminine describing forms.

example.es: Levanta la mano derecha.
example.en: Raise your right hand.

cards.noteEn: With mano, firme describes a hand that does not shake and can make precise movements.

example.es: Dibuja la línea con mano firme.
example.en: Draw the line with a steady hand.

cards.answerEn: excuse me; forgive me (said to several familiar people)
cards.noteEn: Perdonad is the positive command used in Spain when addressing more than one familiar listener. Me attaches to it and identifies the speaker asking to be excused.

example.es: Perdonadme, llego tarde.
example.en: Excuse me, I am late.

cards.answerEn: the idea that a very small change can lead to much larger later differences in a chaotic system
cards.noteEn: The phrase is associated with weather and chaos theory. The comic literalizes it by treating one butterfly wingbeat as a disturbance that can be controlled precisely through the atmosphere.

cards.promptEs: dejar que otra persona haga algo
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone lets or allows another person to do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of dejar, then que, then put the allowed action in its special requested-action form; state the person when the context does not already make them clear.
cards.noteEn: That special form is called the subjunctive because the action is being allowed or requested, not stated as an established fact. For example, ordinary decide changes to decida, and ordinary busco changes to busque. The person can be explicit, as in deja que Ana decida, or understood from the action form and situation, as in deja que busque, “let me search.” Dejar changes for the person and time; que remains unchanged.

example.es: Deja que Ana decida.
example.en: Let Ana decide.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links dejar to the allowed action
cards.noteEn: After a form of dejar meaning “let” or “allow,” que introduces the allowed action. The person doing that action may be stated after que or understood from the situation and the verb form.

example.es: Dejamos que Ana elija.
example.en: We let Ana choose.

cards.answerEn: it flaps (special form after dejan que)
cards.noteEn: Bata comes from batir. Ordinary bate states that it flaps; after dejar que, bata presents the flapping as the action being allowed. The special form is called the subjunctive.

example.es: Deja que el pájaro bata las alas.
example.en: Let the bird flap its wings.

cards.noteEn: Sus agrees with the plural things owned, not with the owner. The same Spanish form can also mean “his,” “her,” or “their” in other contexts, so context identifies the owner.

example.es: El árbol pierde sus hojas.
example.en: The tree loses its leaves.

cards.noteEn: Here una gives the number of occasions rather than introducing an unspecified thing.

example.es: Lo intenté una vez.
example.en: I tried it once.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; marks propagarse, “to spread”
cards.noteEn: Propagarse describes something spreading or traveling outward without naming an outside agent that spreads it. Se stays before the changed form of propagar.

example.es: El sonido se propaga por el aire.
example.en: Sound travels through the air.

cards.noteEn: Bolsa usually means a bag. In scientific descriptions, a bolsa de aire is a bounded pocket or localized mass of air.

example.es: Hay bolsas de aire frío en el valle.
example.en: There are pockets of cold air in the valley.

cards.noteEn: Spanish can use a before a measured or described physical condition, as in a alta presión or a baja temperatura.

example.es: El gas está a alta presión.
example.en: The gas is at high pressure.

cards.noteEn: Que connects a noun to information describing it. Depending on the noun, English translates it as “who,” “that,” or “which.”

example.es: La persona que llamó es mi amiga.
example.en: The person who called is my friend.

cards.noteEn: A rayo can be a ray or beam of radiation, a lightning bolt, or a sudden streak. The scientific labels here use the radiation sense.

example.es: Los rayos atraviesan el material.
example.en: The rays pass through the material.

cards.promptEs: cambio de bit por un rayo cósmico
cards.answerEn: energetic radiation can disturb electronics and accidentally change a stored bit
cards.noteEn: Cosmic rays can contribute to rare hardware errors called bit flips. The absurd step in the comic is focusing one through the atmosphere so that it strikes a chosen drive platter and changes exactly the desired bit.
Cósmico describes something related to the cosmos or outer space. The ending changes to match the noun.

example.es: El detector registra rayos cósmicos.
example.en: The detector records cosmic rays.

cards.noteEn: Enfocando is the ongoing-action form of enfocar, “to focus.” Los attaches to the end and means “them,” referring to masculine plural things.

example.es: Ajusta los rayos enfocándolos en un punto.
example.en: Adjust the rays by focusing them on one point.

cards.answerEn: so that (before que and a desired result)
cards.noteEn: Before que and a full event, para introduces the purpose of an action. Translate para que together as ‘so that’ or ‘in order that.’

example.es: Hablo despacio para que todos entiendan.
example.en: I speak slowly so that everyone understands.

cards.questionEn: How do you express a purpose when someone or something else carries out the desired result?
cards.answerEn: Use para que, then put the result verb in the special form used for a purpose that is not yet a fact.
cards.noteEn: That special form is called the subjunctive. It appears because the second action is intended or desired, not presented as an established fact. For example, ordinary ve becomes vea, and ordinary viene becomes venga. Use para plus an unchanged action verb instead when the same person performs both actions.

example.es: Dejo una nota para que Ana la vea.
example.en: I leave a note so that Ana sees it.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; completes para que, ‘so that’
cards.noteEn: Que completes the purpose connector para que before an event with its own person or thing carrying out the action.

example.es: Cierra la puerta para que no entre frío.
example.en: Close the door so that cold air does not come in.

cards.answerEn: they hit; strike (special purpose form after para que)
cards.noteEn: Incidan comes from incidir. Ordinary inciden states that several things strike a surface; after para que, incidan presents that impact as the intended result. The special form is called the subjunctive.

example.es: Mueve el espejo para que los rayos incidan aquí.
example.en: Move the mirror so that the rays hit here.

cards.answerEn: platter (the magnetic disk inside a drive)
cards.noteEn: Plato normally means a plate or dish. In computer hardware, a plato is one of the flat circular surfaces on which a hard drive stores data.

example.es: El disco tiene dos platos magnéticos.
example.en: The disk has two magnetic platters.

cards.noteEn: In computing, unidad can mean a storage drive, as in unidad de disco. This is different from the general meaning “unit.”

example.es: La unidad guarda una copia del archivo.
example.en: The drive stores a copy of the file.

cards.answerEn: they change; flip (a bit, special purpose form)
cards.noteEn: Ordinary cambian states that several things change something. Cambien is the special form used here because it remains inside the intended result introduced by para que.

example.es: Ajusta el sistema para que cambien el valor.
example.en: Adjust the system so that they change the value.

cards.noteEn: A bit is the smallest ordinary unit of digital information and has one of two values, conventionally 0 or 1.

example.es: Ese bit cambia de cero a uno.
example.en: That bit changes from zero to one.

cards.noteEn: Used by itself as a reaction, bonito can approve something as pleasing or impressive rather than describe a specific masculine noun.

example.es: —Mira mi dibujo. —Bonito.
example.en: —Look at my drawing. —Nice.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; part of por supuesto (“of course”)

cards.questionEn: How do you say “of course” when something is obvious or agreed?
cards.noteEn: Por supuesto is a fixed expression. It can confirm a request or emphasize that the speaker sees something as expected.

example.es: Por supuesto, puedes entrar.
example.en: Of course, you can come in.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; part of por supuesto (“of course”)
command (an instruction given to a computer)
Use para followed by the verb’s dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form ends in -ar, -er, or -ir and is called the infinitive. Use para + verb when the same person or thing performs both actions: in estudio para aprender, I both study and learn. When someone else performs the second action, Spanish needs the different pattern para que.
cards.questionEn: How do you say “in order to do something” in Spanish?

example.es: Estudio para aprender.
example.en: I study in order to learn.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word here; article before the name of a command
cards.noteEn: A masculine noun such as comando can remain understood before its specific name, while el still appears. Natural English often gives the command name directly without “the.”

example.es: Usa el comando Guardar.
example.en: Use the Save command.

cards.noteEn: Before the name of a familiar thing, viejo can express affectionate or nostalgic familiarity. It need not literally claim that the thing is physically old.

example.es: Volvamos al viejo método de siempre.
example.en: Let us return to the good old usual method.

cards.noteEn: Before a noun, maldito can express strong anger or contempt. It is rude or emotionally charged.

example.es: ¿Dónde está el maldito informe?
example.en: Where is the damn report?
